title: adaptive-nccl-throttler-and-kvcache-slicing-to-reduce-comm-stalls-in-tp
author: Ivy Chen
release_notes: Introduce an adaptive NCCL throttler and KV-cache slice manager to improve overlap of communication and compute on tensor-parallel workloads; exposes runtime knobs for aggressive/ conservative throttling; improves p95 latency and throughput on multi-GPU jobs; configurable rollback via feature flag.
description: Motivation: On multi-GPU tensor-parallel (TP) inference we observe intermittent comm stalls when large KV cache synchronization coincides with heavyweight collective traffic. These stalls inflate p95 latency and reduce sustained throughput for long-sequence workloads. This PR implements two coordinated runtime improvements: 1) an adaptive NCCL throttler that dynamically paces collective progress across TP ranks based on recent stream congestion metrics and bandwidth headroom estimates; 2) a KV-cache slicer that splits large KV synchronizations into size-aware shards and schedules them colocated with low-priority collectives so they can be interleaved with compute. Design: The NCCL throttler monitors per-stream counters (bytes_in_flight, op_latency_histogram) and computes a throttle_factor per-node which is translated into a lightweight MPI-like backoff token that delays lower-priority collectives for up to a configurable window. The KV-cache slicer computes shard boundaries keyed to tensor-parallel shard layout and sequence-length distribution, emitting incremental allgather fragments that respect ordering constraints. Both subsystems expose runtime feature flags and thresholds via the existing config layer so customer deployments can toggle aggressive vs conservative modes. Implementation: Changes are split across runtime/collectives (src/runtime/collectives/nccl_throttle.cc, nccl_throttle.h, test harnesses), runtime/kv_cache (src/runtime/kv_cache/slicer.{cc,h}), and the interleaved dispatcher scheduler (src/runtime/scheduler/interleaved_dispatcher.cpp) which integrates token-based pacing. Added unit and integration tests (tests/unit/nccl_throttle_test.cc, tests/integration/tp_kvcache_slice.py) and a benchmark harness (benchmarks/tp_throughput/bench_throttle.py). Performance: Microbenchmarks on a 4xA100 TPU-equivalent cluster show 18–22% p95 latency reduction for opt-13b-like models at 2k sequence lengths under mixed request sizes; stress testing at 16 GPUs shows up to 32% throughput improvement in sustained QPS with long-context workloads. Rollout plan: behind feature flag 'adaptive_nccl_throttle' in main config, rollout to Dedicated clusters as an A/B experiment then opt-in for Hosted after 2 weeks of stability metrics. Rollback: feature flag off and fallback to existing static-priority collectives. Checklist: - [x] design doc linked and reviewed (ENG-4117) - [x] unit tests for throttle heuristics - [x] integration tests across 2/4/8 GPU configs - [x] perf harness and reproducible benchmark runbooks - [x] observability: expose throttle_factor and shard_progress metrics - [x] docs: short guide and recommended knobs (docs/perf/nccl_tuning.md) Related work: complements earlier NCCL stream coalescing and priority-stream experiments (see ENG-3782). This PR is intentionally conservative about default thresholds to avoid unexpected perf regressions in heterogenous clouds.

feat(kv-cache): implement slicer and incremental allgather fragments

ci_details: CI: integration (2xA100 emu) — pass after rerun
Perf regression check — no regression detected
notes_for_operators: Feature is behind 'adaptive_nccl_throttle' flag and 'kvcache_slicing' flag. Recommended default: adaptive_nccl_throttle=false on heterogeneous clusters until validated; kvcache_slicing=true safe for most long-context workloads. Metrics introduced: runtime.throttle_factor, runtime.kvcache_shard_progress, runtime.bytes_in_flight_histogram. If regressions observed set both flags false and notify infra@redwood.
bench_summary: 4xA100: p95 down 18–22% on long-context; 16-GPU sustained throughput +32% on targeted TP configs. Memory overhead: <1.5% for slice metadata; CPU scheduler overhead: ~3–6% at 1k qps which is offset by reduced stall time.
manual_test_plan: 1) Enable feature flags in staging with small Dedicated cluster (4 GPUs). 2) Run bench_throttle on opt-13b-like model at 512/1024/2048 seq lengths. 3) Validate metrics for throttle_factor and shard_progress. 4) Run long-running workload for 48h to observe stability. 5) If stable, promote to A/B on Dedicated for 14 days.
incident_correlation: Related to recent spike during SUP-9021 where KV-sync at seq>2k caused p99 regressions on Dedicated; this PR addresses the root cause by breaking up large syncs and pacing collectives.
